chk_problem.reason: Both drafts identify prefix entanglement in the transformer KV cache as the problem, which prevents exact context reuse and deletion.

chk_method.reason: Both drafts describe the SMem architecture, highlighting block-local/independent encoding and a cross-attention reader.

chk_data.reason: Both drafts identify the FineWeb-Edu dataset, with Draft B providing additional details on token counts and model scales.

chk_setup.reason: Both drafts describe the pretraining setup on FineWeb-Edu with matched parameters.

chk_primary_result.reason: Both drafts report the same needle retrieval accuracy of 0.14–0.28 at 4× training length (distances of 31 and 63 blocks).

chk_secondary_result.reason: Draft A focuses on the perplexity gap compared to standard transformers, while Draft B focuses on the reduction in Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and serving costs.

chk_baseline.reason: Both drafts list the same baselines, including standard/learned-position transformers, RoPE transformers, and Block-Attention variants.

chk_conclusion.reason: Both drafts conclude that SMem achieves comparable perplexity to transformers while enabling exact memory operations.

chk_limitation.reason: Both drafts identify that SMem requires pretraining (cannot be retrofitted) and has sensitivity/gaps in performance depending on the recipe.
